hello.note: The reply is Dia is Muire duit. To several people: Dia daoibh. Casually: haigh.

goodbye.note: If you are leaving, say slán agat; to someone who is leaving, slán leat.

please.note: To several people: le bhur dtoil.

thank_you.note: To several people: go raibh maith agaibh. Thanks a million: go raibh míle maith agat.

youre_welcome.note: Also very common: ná habair é (don't mention it) or níl a bhuíochas ort.

yes.note: Irish has no true word for yes; you echo the verb: An bhfuil tú réidh? – Tá. Sea is the general form.

no.note: Usually you echo the verb: An bhfuil tú réidh? – Níl. Ní hea is the general form.

sorry.note: For a small slip or bump, gabh mo leithscéal is also common.

excuse_me.note: Said roughly 'gow muh lesh-kayl'. To several people: gabhaigí mo leithscéal.

good_morning.note: Also: Dia duit ar maidin. Traditionally Dia duit serves at any time of day.

how_are_you.note: Connacht: Cén chaoi a bhfuil tú? Ulster: Cad é mar atá tú? Irish uses tú for everyone.

im_fine.text: Tá mé go maith, go raibh maith agat
im_fine.note: In Munster: Táim go maith. Also: go breá (fine) or ar fheabhas (great).

whats_your_name.note: Connacht: Cén t-ainm atá ort? Ulster: Cad é an t-ainm atá ort?

my_name_is.note: The name comes first: Seán is ainm dom. Also common: Is mise Seán.

nice_to_meet_you.note: Also common: is deas bualadh leat. In Connacht: castáil leat instead of bualadh leat.

where_from.note: Also heard: Cé as thú? (Connacht), Cad as duit? (Munster).

im_from.note: E.g. Is as Éirinn mé. Countries with 'an' change: Is as an bhFrainc mé (France).

speak_english.note: Irish says you 'have' a language. Also heard: An labhraíonn tú Béarla?

dont_understand.note: Said roughly 'nee hig-im'. Ní thuigim thú = I don't understand you.

speak_slowly.text: Labhair níos moille, le do thoil
speak_slowly.note: To several people: labhraígí níos moille. Softer: An bhféadfá labhairt níos moille?

where.note: Before a verb it is just cá: Cá bhfuil sé? (Where is it?)

what.note: Connacht: Céard? Ulster: Cad é? To mean 'pardon?', say gabh mo leithscéal?

who.note: Usually with more: Cé hé sin? (who's that – a man), Cé hí sin? (a woman).

how_much.note: Ulster: Cá mhéad atá air seo?

where_bathroom.text: Cá bhfuil an leithreas, le do thoil?
where_bathroom.note: On toilet doors: Fir = men, Mná = women.

can_you_help.note: More polite: An bhféadfá cabhrú liom? Ulster uses cuidiú for cabhrú.

what_time.note: Answer: Tá sé a trí a chlog (It's three o'clock).

what_means.note: Also: Cad a chiallaíonn sé seo? For a word: Cad is brí leis an bhfocal seo?

one.note: Counting form. With a noun: noun + amháin, e.g. cupán amháin (one cup).

two.note: With a noun: dhá, e.g. dhá chupán (two cups).

three.note: Counting people uses special forms: beirt (two people), triúr (three people).

four.note: With a noun: ceithre, e.g. ceithre chupán (four cups).

six.note: Said 'shay': s before e or i sounds like 'sh'.

seven.note: Said roughly 'shakht'. With a noun: seacht gcupán (seven cups).

eight.note: The h is only for counting; with a noun: ocht gcupán (eight cups).

ten.note: With a noun: deich gcupán (ten cups).

water.note: Said 'ish-ka'. Whiskey comes from uisce beatha, 'water of life'.

tea.note: Said 'tay'. A cup of tea: cupán tae.

im_hungry.note: Literally 'hunger is on me': many feelings are 'on' you in Irish.

bill_please.note: Also: an cuntas, le do thoil.

no_meat.note: I'm a vegetarian: is feoilséantóir mé.

enjoy_meal.note: To several people: bainigí taitneamh as bhur mbéile!

left.note: Turn left: cas ar chlé. Also written ar clé.

right.note: Turn right: cas ar dheis. On your right: ar do dheis.

straight_ahead.note: Also: díreach romhat (straight in front of you).

stop_here.note: Also: stad anseo, le do thoil.

want_to_go.note: Before 'the', use go dtí: Ba mhaith liom dul go dtí an t-aerfort.

is_it_far.text: An bhfuil sé i bhfad ó seo?
is_it_far.note: Answers: tá (it is) or níl (it isn't).

too_expensive.note: Ró- means 'too', as in rómhór (too big).

cheaper.text: An bhfuil aon rud níos saoire agat?

id_like_this.text: Ba mhaith liom é seo, le do thoil

just_looking.text: Níl mé ach ag féachaint thart
just_looking.note: Connacht: ag breathnú thart; Ulster: ag amharc thart.

pay_card.text: An féidir liom íoc le cárta?

cash.note: Literally 'dry money'. Paying in cash: ag íoc le hairgead tirim.

later.note: In speech also: ar ball (in a while).

good_evening.note: Many speakers simply say Dia duit at any hour.

see_you_later.note: Also: slán go fóill (bye for now).

wait_moment.note: To several people: fanaigí nóiméad. Also: fan go fóill.

call_police.note: In Ireland the police are the Gardaí; elsewhere say na póilíní.

need_doctor.note: Also: teastaíonn dochtúir uaim. Ulster: tá dochtúir de dhíth orm.

dont_feel_well.note: Simpler: níl mé go maith. I'm sick: tá mé tinn.

lost_phone.note: Also: chaill mé mo ghuthán (the Ulster word).

allergic.note: E.g. Tá ailléirge orm le cnónna (nuts).

be_careful.note: Watch out!: Seachain! To several people: bígí cúramach!

i_like_it.note: For a feminine noun: is maith liom í.

dont_like_it.note: For a feminine noun: ní maith liom í.

welcome.note: The famous warm version: Céad míle fáilte! To several guests: fáilte romhaibh!

my_family.note: Mo (my) softens teaghlach to theaghlach. Also: mo mhuintir (my people, my folks).

mother.note: Mum: mam or mamaí. My mother: mo mháthair.

father.note: Dad: daid or daidí. My father: m'athair.

brother.note: Said roughly 'dreh-hawr'. My brother: mo dheartháir.

sister.note: Said roughly 'dreh-fyoor'. My sister: mo dheirfiúr.

child.note: Son: mac. Daughter: iníon. Also: leanbh (child, baby).

friend.note: Same word for a female friend. My friend: mo chara.

this_is_my_friend.note: For a female friend: Seo í mo chara.

are_you_married.note: Answers: tá (I am) or níl (I'm not).

monday.note: Said roughly 'day loo-in'. Every Monday: gach Luan.

tuesday.note: Named after Mars, like French mardi.

wednesday.note: Said roughly 'day kay-deen'. Céadaoin means 'first fast'.

thursday.note: Written as one word, unlike the other days. Said roughly 'dayr-deen'.

friday.note: Said roughly 'day hee-nyeh'. Aoine means 'fast': the old meatless day.

weekend.note: This weekend: an deireadh seachtaine seo.

what_day.note: Answer e.g. Inniu an Luan (Today is Monday). Also: Cén lá é inniu?

next_week.note: Last week: an tseachtain seo caite.

eleven.note: With a noun: aon chupán déag (eleven cups).

twelve.note: With a noun: dhá chupán déag (twelve cups).

fifteen.note: With a noun: cúig chupán déag (fifteen cups).

twenty.note: Said roughly 'fih-heh'. No a before the tens. Twenty-one: fiche a haon.

thirty.note: The older style is still heard in speech: deich is fiche (ten and twenty).

hundred.note: Said 'kayd', as in céad míle fáilte (a hundred thousand welcomes).

how_old.note: Also common: Cén aois atá tú?

years_old.note: E.g. Tá mé fiche bliain d'aois. After 3–6 say bliana; after 7–10, mbliana.

red.note: Said roughly 'jar-ug'. Red hair is rua, not dearg.

green.note: Glas is nature's green (grass, fields); for bright, artificial green many say uaine.

black.note: Said roughly 'duv'. Dublin comes from Dubh Linn, 'black pool'.

what_colour.note: For a feminine noun: Cén dath atá uirthi?

this_one.note: Ceann stands in for the noun, like 'one' in English.

that_one.note: That one over there: an ceann sin thall.

another_one.note: Same again (e.g. drinks): an rud céanna arís, le do thoil.

its_hot.note: Very hot: tá sé an-te. Scorching: tá sé ag scoilteadh na gcloch (splitting the stones).

its_cold.note: Very cold: tá sé an-fhuar. I'm cold: tá fuacht orm.

its_raining.note: Also: tá sé ag báisteach. Pouring: tá sé ag stealladh báistí.

its_windy.note: Very windy: tá gaoth mhór ann.

weather_today.note: Connacht: Cén chaoi a bhfuil an aimsir inniu? Ulster: Cad é mar atá an aimsir inniu?

beautiful_day.note: The classic small-talk line: Lá breá! (A fine day!)

summer.note: Said roughly 'sow-ruh'. In summer: sa samhradh.

have_reservation.note: Also: tá seomra curtha in áirithe agam (I've booked a room).

room.note: Said roughly 'shohm-ruh'. A single room: seomra singil; a double: seomra dúbailte.

wifi_password.text: Cén pasfhocal atá ar an Wi-Fi?
wifi_password.note: The fh in pasfhocal is silent: said roughly 'pass-ock-ul'.

check_out_time.text: Cén t-am a chaithfidh mé an seomra a fhágáil?

bus.note: By bus: ar an mbus (said 'ar un mus').

next_train.text: Cathain a imeoidh an chéad traein eile?
next_train.note: An chéad … eile = the next …: an chéad bhus eile (the next bus).

is_this_seat_free.text: An bhfuil an suíochán seo saor?
is_this_seat_free.note: Also natural: An bhfuil aon duine ina shuí anseo? (Is anyone sitting here?)

i_work_in.note: E.g. Tá mé ag obair i mbanc (i adds m before b). Before a vowel use in: in oifig.

im_student.note: Women usually say it too, though iníon léinn is also heard. Said roughly 'mock layn'.

meeting.note: Said roughly 'krin-yoo'. I have a meeting: tá cruinniú agam.

day_off.note: I have a day off tomorrow: tá lá saor agam amárach.

colleague.note: Same word for a woman. Said roughly 'koh-ghlak-ee': the gh is a soft, throaty sound, not a hard g.

lets_start.note: Also common: Ar aghaidh linn! (Off we go!)

good_job.note: Also: obair mhaith! Very common too: maith an fear! (to a man), maith an cailín! (to a woman).

table_for_two.text: Bord do bheirt, le do thoil
table_for_two.note: Beirt means 'two people'. For three: bord do thriúr.

what_recommend.note: Connacht: Céard a mholfá dom? Ulster: Cad é a mholfá dom?

not_spicy.text: Gan é a bheith spíosrach, le do thoil
not_spicy.note: Te ('hot') also works: gan é a bheith róthe (not too hot).

vegetarian_food.note: In speech also: bia gan feoil (food without meat).

more_water.note: Tuilleadh = more (of something): tuilleadh aráin (more bread).

no_sugar.note: With milk: le bainne. Black coffee: caife dubh.

im_full.note: Literally 'I've eaten my fill'. Shorter: tá mé lán or tá mé sách.

takeaway.text: Le tabhairt liom, le do thoil
takeaway.note: Takeaway food is bia beir leat.

it_was_delicious.note: Also: bhí sé go hálainn (it was lovely).

keep_change.note: After an the s is silent: said roughly 'un tone-shawl'.

head.note: Said roughly 'kyown'. Also means 'one', as in an ceann seo (this one).

stomach.note: Said roughly 'bul-ug'. Stomach ache: tinneas boilg.

head_hurts.note: Literally 'head-sickness is on me'. Also: tá pian i mo cheann.

have_fever.note: A temperature: tá teocht ard orm.

medicine.note: Hence cógaslann (pharmacy). Also: leigheas. Pills: piollaí or táibléid.

call_ambulance.note: Otharcharr literally means 'patient car'. In Ireland dial 112 or 999.

need_rest.text: Caithfidh mé mo scíth a ligean
need_rest.note: Also: tá scíth uaim (I need a rest).

feel_better.note: Also: tá mé níos fearr anois.

get_well.note: Fuller: Go dtaga biseach ort go luath!

lets_meet.note: As a question: An mbuailfimid le chéile? (Shall we meet up?)

are_you_free.note: Irish uses 'will you be' with tomorrow. Answers: beidh (yes) or ní bheidh (no).

call_me.note: Also: glaoigh orm. Ulster: cuir scairt orm.

your_number.note: The fh is silent. Often heard as uimhir fóin. Ulster: Cén uimhir ghutháin atá agat?

see_you_soon.note: The thú (you) goes at the end, as in feicfidh mé ar ball thú.

have_nice_day.note: To several people: bíodh lá maith agaibh!

good_luck.note: To several people: go n-éirí libh! Also very common: ádh mór!

happy_birthday.note: Also very common: Lá breithe sona duit!

thanks_a_lot.note: Míle (a thousand) makes it stronger. To several people: go raibh míle maith agaibh.

miss_you.note: Also: airím uaim thú (Munster), or is fada liom uaim thú.
